content.thinking:
I'm tracing the causal chain: account page requests failed with a ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47, which happened because the monthly-spend-feature flag was switched on, triggering that code path.

I'm checking for other possible causes — looking at deploy history to confirm nothing else changed around that time, and confirming the flag toggle is the only relevant event, with the later revert bringing the service back to health as corroboration. The deeper cause is that the function divides total spend by purchase count for the month, which is zero for shoppers who hadn't purchased yet that month — though this specific reading hasn't been directly verified, so I need to flag it as unconfirmed.

I'm also noting the error pattern ramped alongside the partial flag rollout — only a fraction of evaluations hit the flag-on path initially before it expanded to all traffic within about a minute. Separately, there's a baseline of unrelated disconnect errors before the incident window that I'm excluding as unrelated. For contributing factors, I'm thinking about the lack of a pre-production check exercising the flag-on path for zero-purchase shoppers, and the fact that the rollout went to full traffic so quickly without a gradual ramp gate.

I'm deciding paging and detection speed aren't real factors here — the alert fired within its normal window and paging wouldn't have sped up Argus's mitigation, so I'll skip those. That leaves me drafting two preventive action items: requiring a flag-on test run before enabling a flag in production, and staging flag rollouts with automatic halts tied to error rate.

The ZeroDivisionError in the no-history path is expected by an existing test, so that's not a real risk, but the division-by-zero in the monthly-spend path is still live with the flag off — re-enabling that flag without a fix would likely break account pages again.

For what went well, Argus correctly reverted the monthly-spend-feature flag after the alert fired, confirmed by the linked events, and the flag history cleanly pins the single change. For what went wrong, nobody was actually paged — there's no on-call incident tied to the alert — so I'll note that gap without attributing it to an AI agent.

As for got lucky, I'm leaning toward leaving it empty since the revert being flag-based and deploy-free was more a matter of design than fortune. For the plain-language cause, I'm framing it as switching on the new monthly-spending feature causing a calculation on account pages to likely divide by zero for shoppers who'd purchased before but not that month, hedging with "likely" since that part rests on weaker evidence while the divide-by-zero itself is confirmed by the logged error.

For root cause, I'm tracing it to the average_spend_per_item_this_month function in spend_summary.py, which throws the ZeroDivisionError when dividing the month's total by a purchase count that's zero for returning-but-inactive-this-month shoppers, with no guard against that case — though I'm wary about citing the specific line number since it introduces a digit I'd rather avoid stating directly.

I also need to avoid other number words like "one" or "single" when describing a single revision or all replicas, rephrasing to "the only" instead. For the causal chain, I'm working out how to phrase the account page error rate spike without using bare numerals, citing the relevant sources while keeping the wording in plain share-of-requests terms.

Next, the failing requests triggered a ZeroDivisionError in spend_summary.py — I'll cite the source but omit the exact line number since there's no clean figure label for it. Then the chain continues: the admin-switched flag enabled evaluations progressively until all were on, rendering account pages broken, whereas before the flag everything worked normally, and reverting it resolved the issue — I'm tracing through the timestamps and sources to confirm this while ruling out deploys as a contributing cause.

I'm also checking whether any other changes occurred in the lead-up, but the provider history shows only this one flag change in the hour before onset, so there's nothing else to rule out. Now I'm identifying the root contributing factor: no test ever exercised account pages for shoppers with zero purchases this month while the monthly-spend feature was active, even though that's described as the ordinary case — meaning this gap in testing let the divide-by-zero bug through undetected.

I'm also flagging a second factor: the rollout flipped from off to on for all evaluations within about a minute, with no staged rollout or automatic revert when errors spiked. From these two gaps I'm drafting action items — requiring the test suite to pass with the flag on before production rollout, staging flag rollouts at small percentages, and auto-reverting when account page errors rise during a rollout.

I'm debating whether lack of paging is a real gap, but since Argus already handled the revert automatically, I'll leave that out rather than add a vague process item. I'm noting a couple of assumptions worth flagging — that the "bought before but not this month" cause rests on unverified data, and that the flag change was an intended admin action — before noting what went well, starting with Argus successfully reverting the monthly-spend feature.

action_items.item: Require the io-shop test suite to pass with a feature flag switched on before that flag can be switched on in production.
Roll out io-shop feature flags in stages, holding at a small share of evaluations before going further.
Turn a flag rollout back automatically when the account page error rate rises while the rollout is in progress.

causal_chain.step: Account pages failed for some shoppers: the share of requests failing rose from {errors_before} before the onset to {errors_at_worst} at its worst, and account page request failures were logged throughout.

The failing account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError in the monthly spend summary in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. This error first appears at the onset and is logged only while the incident lasted.

ruled_out.what: A deploy: none came back for the day before the onset, and the only production change read was this flag switch.
Another flag change: the flag provider's history showed only this change by anyone other than Argus in the hour before.

causal_chain.step: That code path ran because admin switched the feature flag monthly-spend-feature on at {P1.1}. Before that, every evaluation was off and account pages rendered normally. From {G971b.1} some evaluations were on, and soon after that all of them were. Argus turned the flag off and the service came back, and that action was judged confirmed.

With the flag on, the monthly path divides the month's spend by the number of purchases flagged as this month. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, that number is {F1.1}. This comes from Code-Fix reading the source and is unverified: nothing ran its tests or its fix.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Switching on a new monthly-spending feature made the shop's account pages run a calculation that crashed by dividing by an empty count of purchases, likely for shoppers who had bought before but nothing this month.

contributing_factors.factor: No check was seen that ran account pages with monthly-spend-feature on, for a shopper who had bought before but not this month, before the flag was switched on in production. Code-Fix's reading says the existing test helper calls such a shopper the ordinary case.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The crash in the monthly path would have been found before the flag reached production shoppers, so turning the flag on would not have broken account pages.

contributing_factors.factor: The flag went from all evaluations off to all on within about a minute. No staged hold and no automatic revert on the account page error rate were seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Fewer shoppers would have hit the failing path before the error rate showed, and the flag could have been turned back sooner.

went_well: Argus turned monthly-spend-feature off {T18.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
The action was judged confirmed {T21.1 - T18.1} after the flag was turned off.
Reading the flag provider's history (T15) and the change events (T9) narrowed the trigger to this flag switch, with no deploy involved.

input.root_cause: With monthly-spend-feature on, account page requests go through the monthly spend summary in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, which raised ZeroDivisionError (G5309). Code-Fix read the source but nothing ran its reading. By that reading, `average_spend_per_item_this_month` divides the month's total by the number of purchases made this month. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, that number is {F1.1}, and nothing in the code guards against it.
input.still_at_risk: The faulty monthly spend calculation is still in the code behind the flag, so switching monthly-spend-feature on again before a fix is in place would likely make account pages fail for the same shoppers again.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for some shoppers
